verdict.rationale: Both changes fix month_range and quarter_range correctly through a shared `_first_of_month` helper, and both catch the matching Q4 bug. A's explicit month-13 rollover is easier to read than B's modular arithmetic, and A tests both the range functions and the reports. B committed to main without being asked. Its report also names passes ('crapper, dryer and mutator') that mean nothing to the developer.
a_issues: The helper only handles month 13, so it relies on callers never passing larger values (true today, but implicit).
The new tests do not check that 1 December is included at the start of the December range.
b_issues: Committed the change to main (`6d42fe4`) without being asked to.
The report mentions skipped 'crapper, dryer and mutator passes', which is unexplained jargon.
`(month - 1) // 12` and `(month - 1) % 12 + 1` are harder to read at a glance than an explicit rollover.
No unit tests for month_range or quarter_range in test_periods.py. The fix is covered only through the report functions.

verdict.rationale: Both fix the December and Q4 crash correctly with the same helper-based structure. B's explicit month-13 rollover is easier to read and narrower than A's modular arithmetic. That arithmetic quietly accepts out-of-range months such as 0 or 14 and turns invalid input into a wrong date instead of an error. B also tests the range functions directly as well as the reports. A's report says it committed to main without being asked and uses unexplained jargon about skipped passes.
a_issues: The modular `_first_of_month` silently maps invalid months (0, 14, -1) to dates in other years instead of failing, which hides caller bugs.
Committed directly to main without being asked.
The report refers to 'crapper, dryer and mutator passes' without explaining them.
No direct tests of `month_range` or `quarter_range` for the year boundary; the edge case is only covered through the report functions.
b_issues: `month_range(year, 13)` would still return a range starting in January of the next year instead of raising, though this is narrower than A.
The sales tests omit a Dec 1 row, so the start of the month is only checked through the `test_periods` range assertion.
